AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To compare the knee performance and pain in athletes with patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) before and after applying Kinesio Tape(®) (KT) on vastus medialis obliquus (VMO) muscle.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Fifteen participants (10 females, five males) with unilateral PFPS were examined and compared under taped and untaped conditions.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: VMO of the involved leg was taped from origin to insertion, with 75% of KT's maximal length tension.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Maximal eccentric and concentric peak torques of quadriceps were measured at 60 and 180°/s angular velocities by an isokinetic dynamometer. Functional performance and pain were evaluated by functional tests (step-down and bilateral squat) and visual analog scale, respectively.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Paired t-test showed statistically significant increase in VMO peak torque and also repetition of step-down test and bilateral squat after using KT. Pain intensity was also decreased significantly following KT application (p < 0.05).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: KT application over VMO can decrease pain and improve the functional performance, generally and quadriceps muscle strength, particularly, in athletes with PFPS. However, more research is needed to evaluate the long-term effects of this therapeutic procedure.
